**Numerical defect:** The previous AVERAGE/AVG avoided overflow by summing each input divided by the count, but every minimum-subnormal contribution could round to zero (for example, averaging two 5e-324 cells). It also lost a small residual when large positive and negative inputs cancelled in sequence. Even-count MEDIAN used a/2+b/2, which also turns the midpoint of two minimum-subnormal values into zero.

**Source correction:** Added a range-safe mean: scale inputs by the largest absolute value, use Neumaier compensation for normalized terms, and accumulate terms whose normalized ratio underflows separately so they survive cancellation. Clamp only floating-point overshoot to the mathematical bound that a mean cannot exceed the largest absolute input. Even-count MEDIAN now uses a scaled midpoint, avoiding overflow and preserving subnormal values. SUM's existing overflow error and the binary64 precision contract remain unchanged.

**Regression and bundle:** Extended tests/smoke_sheet_numeric_hardening.py with raw workbook-range checks for subnormal AVERAGE/AVG/MEDIAN, negative subnormal median, adjacent subnormal midpoint, a three-Number.MAX_VALUE mean, and cancellation of 1e308 + (-1e308) while retaining the 1e-300 residual. The test also round-trips the aggregate workbook and restores the original workbook. Updated docs/DATA_TABLES.md. Updated src/data-tables.js and the matching inline module in standalone index.html in the same commit; source/bundle module parity was checked before and after the edit.

**Validation:** Isolated V8 checks passed for minimum-subnormal means/medians, adjacent-subnormal midpoint, opposite maximum values, maximum-value average, and cancellation residual. **P1 numerical defect:** L-angle principal inertia used a normalized 2×2 determinant to recover the minor eigenvalue. For B=1e100 mm, H=1e-139 mm and t=1e-140 mm, the normalized Ixx and Ixy both underflow to zero relative to Iyy, so the normalized determinant is zero even though the physical minor principal moment is still representable as a positive subnormal. The section's area, centroidal moments, major/minor principal moments, section moduli and radii remain finite.

**Source correction:** tools/truss-fem.js keeps the normalized determinant path when it yields a positive finite minor moment. If that path underflows/non-finite, it now tries the unscaled determinant Ixx*Iyy-Ixy² only when that determinant is finite and positive, then divides by the already-computed major eigenvalue. If neither path can produce a positive finite result, the existing explicit underflow error remains. No section geometry, solver, model or member-application behavior changed.

**Regression:** tests/test_truss_fem.js proves the normalized determinant is exactly zero for the synthetic geometry, then checks the returned minor principal moment against a 100-digit Decimal reference evaluated from the exact binary64 dimensions (rounding to 8.35e-322 mm⁴). It also verifies positive finite major moment, section moduli, radii and angle, nonzero product of inertia, unchanged inputs and immutable output. tests/smoke_truss_fem.py exercises the same engine through Chromium at 1280px and 390px and checks the subnormal result plus all other finite section outputs.

It computes (I=(\pi/64)D_o^2 f_I D_o^2), placing the dimensionless annulus factor between the two finite (D_o^2) factors. The solid-circle path retains its direct fourth-power finite guard. Existing geometry validation, thin-wall cancellation protection and underflow/finite-result checks remain intact.

## 2026-11-24 — TRUSS-COMPOSITE-SECTION-MOMENT-OVERFLOW-SAFETY

**Starting refs:** dev 61ea34c025f169ea235611fbed99560d7f503e4b; main 70fc483cb1cec3d2372d37484e4a8ef7942343da. Re-read root AGENTS.md, this plan, the frozen 2026-10-26 inventory, Structural Truss contract/source/tests, PR #189/reviews, branch refs, exact-head Actions and main Quality/Pages evidence.

**P0 CI baseline:** Exact-head Push Quality [#45303082063](https://github.com/saeedsai/ProMathStudio/actions/runs/45303082063) and PR Quality [#45303087913](https://github.com/saeedsai/ProMathStudio/actions/runs/45303087913) both passed 218/218 steps, zero failures and zero skipped steps. The FEM Node/browser and existing Truss Studio regressions are green on the starting SHA.

**P1 numerical defect:** The local rectangle moments in composite channel, I-section and L-angle decompositions were evaluated left-to-right as b*h*h*h/12 and h*b*b*b/12. Floating-point multiplication can overflow before division even when the final local moment is finite. For example, a channel web with b=1e74 mm and h=2e78 mm has a finite Decimal-reference Ixx, but the previous intermediate b*h^3 becomes Infinity before /12.

**Source fix:** tools/truss-fem.js now evaluates the same exact formulas in an overflow-aware order: (b*h)*(h/12)*h and (b*h)*(b/12)*b. Shared local-rectangle helpers are used by both the composite and L-angle decompositions. No solver stiffness, load, displacement, parallel-axis term, centroid, normal-size result or import contract changed.

**Regression:** tests/test_truss_fem.js adds 120-digit Decimal references (evaluated from exact binary64 inputs) for extreme-range channel, I-section and L-angle cases. It first proves the previous multiplication order overflows, then checks finite positive area, centroid, Ixx/Iyy, section moduli, radii and L-angle principal moments within relative tolerance 2e-13. These dimensions are synthetic floating-range stress cases, not practical engineering sizes.

**Validation:** Isolated Node 22 formula checks reproduced the old overflow and matched channel/I-section references after reordering. Independent 120-digit Decimal references were calculated for all three shapes. The execution workspace has no repository checkout, so the complete local Node and Chromium suites could not run; fresh exact-head Push/PR Quality is required. Candidate is Implemented on dev / In QA, not released.

## 2026-11-23 — TRUSS-L-ANGLE-STABLE-PRINCIPAL-MOMENT (implemented on dev; exact-head QA pending)

Starting refs: dev c12e41e5c340a2ebcb2e0c6c3e311071b67db61b, main 70fc483cb1cec3d2372d37484e4a8ef7942343da. Re-read root AGENTS.md, this plan, the frozen October 26 inventory, Truss FEM source/tests/contract, PR #189 and reviews, current refs, exact-head Actions and main Quality/Pages evidence.

Each completed all **218/218 steps**, with zero failures and zero skipped steps. Truss Studio 212, FEM analytical 214 and FEM browser/mobile 215 all passed. No failing exact-head CI defect remained at the start of this iteration.

**P1 numerical defect:** L-angle principal moments were computed as mean ± radius in the unscaled inertia tensor. For a valid slender angle (B=1,000,000 mm, H=1 mm, t=0.001 mm), the true positive minor principal moment is approximately 4.161659185863228e-4 mm⁴, but floating-point subtraction of two nearly equal large terms rounded it to zero and incorrectly rejected the section as underflow. The geometry, area and centroid are representable; this is avoidable eigenvalue cancellation, not an invalid section.

**Source correction:** Normalize Ixx, Iyy and Ixy by their maximum magnitude before computing the symmetric 2×2 eigenvalues. Compute I1 from normalized mean + radius and I2 from the normalized determinant divided by the normalized I1. Compute the principal-axis angle from the normalized tensor as well, avoiding overflow in the unscaled sum and doubled Ixy. Retain explicit finite and strictly-positive checks; do not clamp invalid determinants or moments.

**Regression:** Added a direct Node test for the 1,000,000 × 1 mm L-angle with 0.001 mm thickness. It checks a high-precision composite-rectangle reference for I2, finite positive I1/I2, principal-axis angle, trace invariant and immutable result. Existing ordinary/asymmetric/near-limit L-angle references remain unchanged.

The model tables previously listened to both `input` and `change`. Changed the editor to use bubbling `input` as the authoritative mutation event for node/member controls, removed the duplicate change-driven invalidation, and moved member-ID selector synchronization into the member-table input handler. Real text/number/checkbox edits still invalidate immediately; explicit Analyze still cancels a pending import. No import validation, solver behavior, units, or CI assertions were weakened.

Extended the Chromium regression in two directions. Second, it holds another read open, performs a real density `input` edit to 8000, requires the cancellation status and `aria-busy=false`, releases the late bytes and verifies the edited 8000 value remains. Updated the Truss contract to document the event contract.

The local checkout is absent and the bounded local Git path remains unavailable due execution-container DNS; the connected GitHub integration is used. ## 2026-11-23 — TRUSS-IMPORT-SELF-CANCELLATION-CI-FIX (implemented on dev; exact-head Quality pending)

Started from dev `21c94497506f63b4e2f4e7accc9cac65d9fe2faa` and main `70fc483cb1cec3d2372d37484e4a8ef7942343da`. Re-read root `AGENTS.md`, this plan, the frozen 2026-10-26 inventory, Structural Truss contract/source/tests, current branch refs, PR #189/reviews, exact-head Actions, rulesets and Pages evidence.

Prioritized the observed exact-head failure. Push Quality [#45092387908](https://github.com/saeedsai/ProMathStudio/actions/runs/45092387908) and PR Quality [#45092393490](https://github.com/saeedsai/ProMathStudio/actions/runs/45092393490) both fail in mandatory Static and browser regression step 212, `tests/smoke_truss_studio.py:701`, after the latest-file import-ordering wait times out. The logs show the structural/static suite and tool-search browser check passed before the Truss Studio browser regression timed out; both workflows fail at the same test line.

Root cause: the importer correctly validates the latest request token, but the successful import then calls `renderModel(model)`. `renderModel()` calls `invalidate()`, and `invalidate()` unconditionally invokes `cancelPendingImport()`. That increments the request token and clears pending state for the very import currently being rendered. The following `finishCurrentImport(request)` therefore rejects its own current request, leaving the new model unanalyzed and the status/busy-state acceptance wait unsatisfied.

Fixed the lifecycle without weakening cancellation: `renderModel(model, preserveImportRequest)` passes the active token to `invalidate(preserveImportRequest)`; invalidation skips cancellation only when the supplied token still matches the latest pending request. All normal calls omit the token and retain the existing behavior that edits, examples and unrelated model replacement cancel pending imports. The importer still calls `finishCurrentImport(request)` after rendering, then analyzes. Stale older requests remain rejected by the monotonic token.

Reworked the Truss Studio latest-file regression in `tests/smoke_truss_studio.py` to use a deterministic per-File deferred read instead of a timer and shared `File.prototype.arrayBuffer` override. It starts an older invalid file, waits until that exact read is pending, imports the valid triangle, and requires the analysis status, `aria-busy=false`, A/B/C joint IDs, AC/BC/AB member IDs, 11.21 m total length and three material rows. Only then does it release the older invalid bytes; the exact success status, model IDs, metrics and busy state must remain unchanged. This directly catches the self-cancellation defect and proves stale failure isolation.

Added pure, immutable solid-section property helpers to the canonical Truss FEM API and a user-facing helper in the standalone Truss Studio. A solid rectangle uses A=b·h and I=b·h³/12 about the centroidal axis parallel to width; a solid circle uses A=πd²/4 and I=πd⁴/64 about a centroidal diameter. Dimensions are in mm, returned area in mm² and I in mm⁴. The UI lets the user select a member, shape and dimensions, then atomically applies both A and I to that member only. Positive finite input is required; underflow/overflow and unsupported shapes are rejected without changing the member. I and K remain independently optional member properties: either may be stored alone, while Pcr is calculated only when both exist, so applying section I does not require guessing an effective-length factor.
